previous_versions.body: > I would like to have clear message, that input validation is not for defense against XSS, SQL injection etc. Input validation is just for (business logic) data integrity. How the data is handled later, is not input validation responsibility. That is not true. You need output validation as a core defense for untrusted URL's. Like in react: `CLICK ME` is solved with URL validation in react, not encoding. Angular has this validation defense built in.
